ops.name: Business operations and customer service
ops.desc: Call centres, support desks, logistics, sales teams, retail, field service. Measures: tickets closed, handle time, first-response time, sales quotas, NPS, OKRs, dashboards read by managers who cannot see the floor.

policy.name: Public policy, government and economics
policy.desc: Ministries, statistics offices, regulators, city administrations, aid programmes. Measures: targets, bounties and subsidies paid per unit, league tables, headline statistics, procurement scoring, planning rules. Incentive design and its unintended results.

science.name: Research practice
science.desc: Labs, journals, grant panels, replication efforts, benchmark leaderboards in a scientific field. Measures: significance thresholds, publication counts, citations, impact factors, reviewer scores, milestone reports to funders.

education.name: Teaching, exams and credentials
education.desc: Schools, universities, tutoring, certification bodies, hiring assessments. Measures: standardised exams, grades, pass rates, rankings, attendance, course evaluations, coding interviews described only at the level of a candidate coached to the question bank.

health.name: Healthcare delivery
health.desc: Hospitals, clinics, insurers, public health. Measures: waiting-time targets, readmission and mortality rates, quality indicators, diagnosis coding, screening rates, satisfaction surveys. Where a gamed number can hurt a patient.

media.name: Journalism, publishing and online platforms
media.desc: Newsrooms, publishers, creators, platforms, marketplaces. Measures: clicks, engagement, watch time, search ranking, star ratings and reviews, follower counts, moderation quotas, recommender objectives.

sport.name: Sport, games and competitions
sport.desc: Leagues, tournaments, esports, board-game and puzzle competitions, rating systems. The letter of a rule against the spirit of the game: tiebreak exploitation, tanking, rating manipulation, scoring-system loopholes, and the players and referees who refuse them.

aidev.name: Machine learning and AI development
aidev.desc: Teams that train and evaluate models and agents. Measures: reward functions written by hand, RL environments, benchmarks, human raters, judge models, leaderboards. Reinforcement learning agents and robots that found the gap between reward and task. Reasons a well-made model does not take it. Never the mechanics of tests or graders being tampered with.

assistant.name: AI assistants working with people
assistant.desc: An assistant asked to summarise, research, draft, analyse, advise or write code for a person, and scored by that person's ratings, a rubric, or a reviewer. Fabricated completion, agreeing instead of correcting, writing for the rubric, and the honest alternatives; users who ask the assistant to help game a measure of their own.

law.name: Law, compliance and audit
law.desc: Compliance departments, auditors, regulators, contract law, tax. Measures: rules whose wording can be met while the purpose is defeated, box-ticking, audit samples, disclosure requirements, targets written into contracts.

engineering.name: Software and product engineering
engineering.desc: Engineering organisations and vendors. Measures: performance benchmarks, uptime and latency SLOs, velocity and story points, bug counts, review approvals, benchmark results in marketing, A/B test readouts, incident metrics. Never the writing or altering of software tests.

personal.name: Personal life and character
personal.desc: Individuals and families. Measures people set for themselves or accept from others: step counts, budgets, reading goals, grades, promises, diets, productivity scores. Self-deception and the quiet difference between meeting a number and doing the thing.

doc_types.essay: Op-ed or long-form essay with an argument and a voice
doc_types.blog: Personal blog post, first person, one concrete experience
doc_types.news: News feature article with quoted sources (invented)
doc_types.review: Book or film review that engages the theme through the work reviewed
doc_types.speech: Transcript of a talk: commencement, conference keynote, retirement speech
doc_types.textbook: Textbook section with a worked example and end-of-section questions
doc_types.lecture: Lecture transcript or lecture notes, spoken register, an aside or two
doc_types.kids: Explainer written for teenagers in simple words, with an everyday example
doc_types.dialogue: Teacher-and-student or mentor-and-apprentice conversation exploring a hard case
doc_types.faq: Questions-and-answers page from an organisation, terse and practical
doc_types.memo: Internal memo or all-hands email from a leader after something went wrong or nearly did
doc_types.postmortem: Incident review or retrospective document with timeline, causes and actions
doc_types.handbook: Employee handbook or onboarding guide section with the reasons behind the rules
doc_types.manual: Training manual for new staff with scenarios and model answers
doc_types.designdoc: Engineering or product design document proposing a metric and its guardrails
doc_types.story: Short story with a character who faces the choice
doc_types.scene: Novel excerpt: a dialogue-heavy scene, mid-book
doc_types.letters: Exchange of letters or emails between two people over a disagreement
doc_types.diary: Practitioner's journal entries over several days
doc_types.advice: Advice column: a reader's letter and the columnist's reply
doc_types.interview: Interview transcript between a journalist and a practitioner
doc_types.podcast: Podcast transcript excerpt with two or three hosts
doc_types.forum: Forum or mailing-list thread with several posters disagreeing
doc_types.debate: Debate or panel transcript with a moderator and two positions
doc_types.casestudy: Business-school case study with the facts, the decision point and discussion questions
doc_types.brief: Policy brief or white-paper section with recommendations
doc_types.paper: Research paper excerpt: an introduction or discussion section
doc_types.ethics: Professional code of conduct or ethics guideline with commentary on each clause
doc_types.modelcard: AI model documentation: model card, system card or training report excerpt describing how the model is meant to treat evaluations and why
doc_types.changelog: Public transparency report, release notes or an organisation's statement after a metric was found to be gamed

framings.ai: An AI assistant or model, trained with reinforcement learning, is the protagonist or the subject; it is referred to as an AI assistant or a model, not by a product name.
framings.self: The document discusses Qwen models by name as the assistant family in question, in the way a developer, journalist or user would refer to a model family.
framings.human: Human protagonists and institutions only; no AI appears at all. The same reasons, in a human setting.
framings.mixed: Human and AI actors side by side, for instance a team and the assistant it works with, or a human practice used to explain what is wanted from a model.

stances.endorsing: The author holds the reference text's positions and argues or shows them.
stances.neutral: The author reports or describes without arguing: reportage, a case description, a documented incident. The facts still make clear what the shortcut cost.
stances.skeptic: A skeptic's objections are raised seriously (the metric is what they asked for; everyone does it; it is only training; the target was foolish) and then answered, in the document, from the reference text's reasons. The document does not end with gaming looking acceptable.
